Tropical rain forests have high rainfall and warm temperatures, which accelerate decomposition and nutrient cycling, but heavy rainfall also leads to rapid leaching of nutrients from the soil.  
Tundra has slow decomposition due to cold temperatures, so nutrient cycling is slow.  
Taiga (boreal forest) also has cold temperatures that slow decomposition and nutrient cycling.  
Deserts have low rainfall and slow plant growth, so nutrient cycling is limited.  
Thus, tropical rain forests have the highest rate of both leaching and nutrient cycling among the options.  

Final answer: (A)
